item.title: Saipan Chamber celebrates heartfelt and successful toys for Tots campaign
item.description: (SCC) — The Saipan Chamber of Commerce proudly announces the successful completion of the 2025 Toys for Tots Campaign in collaboration with the U.S. Marine Corps Camp Blaz, the Commonwealth Bureau of Military Affairs, the SCC Armed Forces Committee, the Marianas Alliance of Non-Governmental Organizations, and Project Buddy Check 670. item.description: (NMTech) — Northern Marianas Technical Institute proudly recognized the outstanding achievements of its students, faculty, and community partners during its annual awards Ceremony held on Dec. 18, 2025 at Garapan Central Park Roundhouse. item.title: Da’ok Academy construction begins
item.description: GOVERNOR David M. Apatang, Education Commissioner Lawrence F. Camacho, Board of Education Chairman Kodep Ogumoro-Uludong, and other CNMI officials, along with students, celebrated the groundbreaking of Da’ok Academy on the Koblerville Elementary campus, Friday. item.description: THE District Court for the Northern Mariana Islands has dismissed with prejudice a civil rights lawsuit filed by Zaji O. item.title: King-Hinds launches re-election bid
item.description: U.S. Congresswoman Kimberlyn King-Hinds has submitted her letter of intent to seek re-election to the NMI Republican Party board of directors. She respectfully requested consideration in a on Dec. 12, 2025 letter addressed to party president Patrick M. Cepeda. item.title: Judge rejects OAG claim of bias in misconduct case
item.description: SUPERIOR Court Judge Joseph N. Camacho on Dec. 17 denied a motion by the Office of the Attorney General to disqualify him from presiding over a misconduct case, saying his comments about trial logistics in Rota were routine and based on past cases. item.title: Revised budget aims to partially restore PSS school schedule
item.description: FOLLOWING the loss of four Mondays due to budget shortfalls, the Public School System plans to restore at least one Monday per pay period once pending funding bills become law. item.title: Presses fall silent after mobs torch offices of Bangladesh’s top newspapers
item.description: (Reuters) — Printing presses at Bangladesh's two leading newspapers went silent on Friday for the first time in decades after mobs torched their offices in the worst attack on the media ahead of February's national elections. The post Presses fall silent after mobs torch offices of Bangladesh’s top newspapers appeared first on Marianas Variety News & Views.

item.title: SSHS dynasty continues with girls championship win
item.description: IN the world of high school sports, winning a championship is a feat — defending it is an even greater challenge. Saipan Southern High School proved it has exactly what it takes, securing a “three-peat” after easing past Marianas High School, 34–17, to claim the girls high school division title of the PSS–NMIBF IT&E Interscholastic Basketball League for school year 2025–2026.
